decisions.reason: The softer, non-calligraphic terminal is owned by the shared terminal Requirement. The request to restore the established Hero V does not establish new geometry values, and its observed loss is already represented as a same-message runtime failure.

Applying the shared terminal proportionally to the second V is already within the source Requirement's scope and is consistent with the candidate's existing derivation from the Hero V; no second-V geometry attribute is changed.
The source asks to reestablish the previously defined VvÉ proportions and hierarchy rather than changing their values. The same-message loss of hierarchy is already represented as runtime evidence.
The source explicitly makes other work secondary and changes only the shared VvÉ terminal treatment and application order; it does not alter the E or L letterform requirements.

Direct application of the finalized Hero V terminal reaffirms the candidate's existing exact literal-derivation rule. The changed terminal language is already represented by the source Requirement and leaves no stale derivation attribute here.
The source does not change the selected champagne finish, color distribution, or any other material-treatment value.
The source changes terminal language but does not change the existing requirement that the Hero V and É accent peaks align exactly.
No clause changes the rule aligning E and L cap height with the second V's left arm.
The source does not revise the selected Balanced Flow kerning or the cohesive-reading objective.
The source contains no change to the common baseline alignment of the wordmark.
The source provides design priorities but does not change the requirement to include rationale with review rounds.
The source does not discuss attachment formats, file accessibility, or Mac-viewable proof delivery.
